Summary
The letter discusses Jack's recent experiences in Manila, including a brief encounter with an old acquaintance, the ongoing rain, and his upcoming inspection trip. Jack also mentions receiving a letter from Ruth and a bundle of clothing from Australia, and expresses hope that Major James will be his replacement. The tone is casual and informative, with a touch of nostalgia and anticipation for future developments.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_91a) --- Dear Falls, Received Ruth's last letter from camp and first letter from the city during the past week. Earlier this evening I ran into the older Pinchinsky boy. Thinks you know his folks. Anyway he didn't recognize me and I had to convince him that he knew me. There's so little to write of that's it pitiful. Everyone is still talking only about young love. [illegible] --- Page 2 (Beckerman_91b) --- are starting to back to the States slowly but surely. all kinds of rumors floating around. I guess that I told you that a Major James over from Wash. ngton who is now walking with me. I'm hoping that he turns out to be my replacement. It has been raining continuously here. Have got to get to bed early tonight since I have to catch a --- Page 3 (Beckerman_91c) --- 3 plane in the morning, Expect to be gone for about a week on an inspection trip. Will be writing you again as soon as I complete the job and return to Manila. Still haven't heard from Abe. Should have word from him in the near future. Ruth, I received your letter addressed to APO 71 without any delay. By the way, did you ever receive a bundle of clothing that I sent home from --- Page 4 (Beckerman_91d) --- Australia, Ruth tells me you are both feeling well and I'm thankful for that. Please keep me informed as to the fellows that are getting home and/or out of the army. That's about all folks. Love Jack
